narrative: Material PL3__M82622E9 exhibits lumpy demand with a high CV of 0.586, driven by intermittent near-zero days interspersed with high-volume working-day draws averaging ~21,961 units/day. Lead times are variable (mean 5.03 days, σ 1.85 days), making lead-time variance the dominant contributor to safety stock requirements. An (r,Q) policy with SS=82,090 and OQ=363,574 was selected to exploit economies of scale in ordering while respecting the 445,664-unit storage cap; the storage constraint binds and caps the EOQ from 499,965 to 363,574 units.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) — Continuous-review fixed-order-quantity with EOQ-derived batch size
research_insights.selection_rationale: High-volume material with known MOQ and lumpy but predominantly positive demand pattern suits a continuous-review (r,Q) model; the EOQ minimises total ordering + holding cost and the MOQ (67,494) is well below the unconstrained EOQ (499,965), so MOQ does not bind — only storage capacity does.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap binds at 445,664 units: unconstrained EOQ 499,965 was reduced to 363,574. During peak demand weeks the reduced OQ increases replenishment frequency slightly, marginally raising stock-out exposure versus the unconstrained optimum. Annual savings remain substantial at 75.2%.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None — MOQ (67,494) + SS (82,090) = 149,584 ≤ max_storage_units (445,664). Policy is fully feasible. No MOQ-capacity conflict.
